title: Antibiotic Resistance
description: Identifying resistant isolates and analyzing soil microbial communities with QIIME 2

blocks.text:
Write a summary of this experiment, its objectives, and conclusions between one
paragraph and one page in length. Specifically, write about the motivation of the
study and what you are looking for with respect to microbial communities in different
soil conditions.


In this experiment, we extracted soil samples from a variety of locations on campus, and tested the microbes for antibiotic resistant bacteria. My team extracted a soil sample from Tournament park near a trash bin, digging 7cm deep near the roots of a plant (likely to be Agapanthus africanus (L.) Hoffmanns - Lily of the nile). Which then the variety of microbes were grown on an agar and individual colonies were isolated. Bacterial colonies were tested for antibiotic resistance, and the microbes were tested for antibiotic producers. Using a DNA soil extraction kit from Qiagen, and the microbial composition was evaluated using QIIME2 taxonomic analysis to reveal high microbial diversity within this localized soil sample. Our aim to to find out how commonly found antibiotic resistant bacteria is in the environment and which commonly used antibiotics they are resistant to. We also tested the soil for antibiotic producers. With antibiotic resistance of bacteria being such a global concern, it is crucial to understand how certain antibiotics work, and how bacteria become resistant to certain antibiotics, and also to discover effective antibiotics that are produced in nature. 


We found a huge variety and diversity of microbes within our sample, and also a few different types of antibiotic resistant bacteria. Lines 3 and 7 were highly resistant to chloramphenicol, line 8 was highly resistant to kanamycin, line 1 was highly resistant to streptomycin and line 1 and 3 were weakly resistant to streptomycin. 

line 8 was analyzed using 16S rRNA BLAST, and was found to be 	Paenibacillus lautus

Found that for our sample, Tournament park by trash bin, we find that our sample has the most archaea compared to other teams, but still at a very low relative frequency compared to bacteria. When we look at level 2, we see that our distribution of Fibrobacteres, Chlamydiae, Chloroflexi and LCP-89 is quite even compared to other teams. There doesn't seem to be any trend when sorting by depth and pH. It is interesing to note that orange walk sample consists almost entirely of gamaproteobacteria and Firmicutes bacteria, showing the least degree of diversity.

But again we see that the sample from orange walk is very different

Expand on the results with any speculations you may have on why you saw the results
you did. You may also posit other hypotheses to test and propose experiments to test
them. You may choose to look into the resistance mechanisms by which a cell can
gain resistance to the antibiotics we used and speculate about how likely it would be
to develop resistance.

Unfortunately there does not seem to be an obvious trend in pH, soil depth etc between the groups. Perhaps a wider range of samples should be taken, outside of the pasadena area, and from a wider range of plants. 

For the antibiotic resistance plates, there is alot of analysis that should be done. 
From blast, Paenibacillus lautus was identified with it's strong resistance to Kanamycin. Paenibacillus lautus is a gram-positive, spore-forming bacterium known for its ability to form endospores, meaning it can survive harsh environmental conditions. Endospores shield bacteria's genetic material, this suggests how it is so resistant to kanamycin, and performing decently with other antibiotics too. It also suggests how Kanamycin works as an antibiotic.

# Put the full path to your home working directory
home_dir = "/Users/curtislee/Documents/Bi1x/Lee_Curtis_5/"

# Subdirectory in home_dir containing all of the reads (probably 'soil')
data_dir = "soil/"

# Whether or not to do pre-processing (this takes a looong time)
# Only change to True if you have not done it yet.
pre_process = True

# Full path to the directory with reads
data_dir = os.path.join(home_dir, data_dir)

# These are artifact and visualization directories located within the home directory.
artifact_dir = os.path.join(home_dir, 'qiime_artifacts/')
visualization_dir = os.path.join(home_dir, 'qiime_visualizations/')

# If these do not exist, make them
if not os.path.exists(artifact_dir):
    os.makedirs(artifact_dir)
    
if not os.path.exists(visualization_dir):
    os.makedirs(visualization_dir)

if pre_process:
    with open(os.path.join(home_dir, 'manifest.txt'), 'w') as f:
        # Add formatting rows
        f.write('sample-id\tforward-absolute-filepath\treverse-absolute-filepath\n')

        # list all files and write the forward reads into the manifest file
        list_of_files = os.listdir(data_dir)  
        forward = '*L001_R1_001.fastq.gz'

        for file in list_of_files:  
            if fnmatch.fnmatch(file, forward):
                line = str(file.split("_")[0]
                           + f'\t{data_dir}'
                           + str(file.split("L001")[0])
                           + 'L001_R1_001.fastq.gz'
                           + f'\t{data_dir}'
                           + str(file.split("L001")[0])
                           + 'L001_R2_001.fastq.gz\n')
                f.write(line)

    pd.set_option('display.max_colwidth', None)           
    pd.read_csv(os.path.join(home_dir, 'manifest.txt'), sep='\t')
